title: From Climate Signals to “Green” Readiness to Act: The Formation of Pro-Environmental Intentions in Russian SMEs
content: Climate change is recognized as one of the key systemic threats to sustainable development, and business engagement in the climate agenda is a prerequisite for achieving the UN Sustainable Development Goals. Given that the Russian Federation experiences climate shifts at a rate exceeding the worldwide mean, coupled with the nascent state of its carbon market regulations, understanding the mechanisms by which small and medium-sized enterprises (SMEs) – with their limited resources and exemption from mandatory regulatory pressure – develop readiness for environmental, and primarily climate-related, action takes on particular significance. Drawing on a qualita-tive abductive research design utilizing the Gioia methodology, this study analyzes ten in-depth semi-structured interviews with owners of Russian SMEs from various industries. Verification was conducted through data triangulation (company websites, media publications, corporate reports) and independent coding. Two distinct trajectories of intention formation were identified: a pragmatic (defensive) trajectory and a value-based (creative) trajectory. A hierarchy of signal extraction and the role of the institutional vacuum as a boundary condition were established. The factors shaping companies' intentions to participate in climate initiatives were verified. Pro-environmental intentions in Russian SMEs are formed not as an automatic reac-tion to external stimuli, but as the result of multi-level cognitive processing in which the owner's personalized initiation interacts with network support, while the institutional vacuum functions simultaneously as both a barrier and a filter.
